caption: Fig. 1. Overview of QEC code synthesis. (a) A ESM circuit for error syndrome extraction. (b) The code topology associated with the ESM circuits. (c) A quantum hardware with sparse architecture. (d) Implementation of swapping-based method. (e) Implementation of swapping-based method with fixed data q

templates.why_chosen: Star, high-confidence double-column matrix with 6 lettered panels sharing one legend on the right: a top row frames a connectivity gap with a bold red arrow and a bottom row compares two solution families.
templates.what_to_learn: Arrange a problem-then-solutions matrix as a top row stating the mismatch and a bottom row of lettered panels comparing candidate fixes, define component colours once in a shared legend at the right edge, and let one bold callout arrow, not a whole panel, carry the gap argument.

templates.why_chosen: Six panels share one legend on the right: the top row frames the code-versus-hardware connectivity gap with a red 'Gap!' arrow, and the bottom row redraws the identical four-qubit circuit to compare swapping against bridging.
templates.what_to_learn: When more than four panels are needed, arrange them as a labelled grid (here 2 rows of 3) with one qubit-colour legend on the side covering every panel, and let a bold callout arrow (the red 'Gap!') point between two panels to name the specific mismatch the rest of the figure resolves.
